triples.relationship: eating and drinking considered in relation to God
triples.rationale: Zechariah challenges people who eat and drink for themselves after questioning their fasts. Paul directs that eating, drinking and everything else be done for God's glory. The contrast concerns the orientation of ordinary consumption toward oneself or toward God.
triples.source_text: If you eat or drink, are you not yourselves eating and yourselves drinking?

target_units.text: Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything, do everything for God’s glory.

triples.relationship: same-book appeal to the words of the former prophets
triples.rationale: Zechariah recalls words spoken through the former prophets when Jerusalem and its surroundings flourished. The opening warning likewise recalls those prophets' calls to turn from evil and the fathers' failure to listen. Both appeal to the earlier prophetic witness in addressing the present community.
triples.source_text: Are these not the words the Lord spoke through the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and flourishing, with her cities around her, and the hill country and plain were inhabited?”

target_units.text: Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.

triples.relationship: righteous public judgment commanded
triples.rationale: Zechariah commands righteous judgment along with mercy toward one's brother. Deuteronomy likewise requires judges to give righteous judgment, forbids its perversion and commands pursuit of justice. Both make just judgment a duty of the community.
triples.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: Render righteous judgment; show mercy and compassion, each to his brother.

target_units.text: You shall appoint judges and recording officers for yourself in all your cities which the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.
You shall pursue justly that which is just, that you may live, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you.

triples.relationship: justice and mercy paired as divine requirements
triples.rationale: Zechariah pairs righteous judgment with mercy and compassion toward one's brother. Micah likewise names doing justice and loving mercy among what the Lord seeks. The two ethical requirements are expressly joined in both passages.
triples.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: Render righteous judgment; show mercy and compassion, each to his brother.

target_units.text: Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?

triples.relationship: prohibition of oppression against the newcomer, orphan and widow
triples.rationale: Zechariah forbids oppressing widow, orphan, newcomer and poor person. Jeremiah likewise forbids oppression of newcomer, orphan and widow within a call to corrected conduct. The three named vulnerable groups and shared prohibition provide the particular connection.
triples.source_text: Do not oppress widow, orphan, newcomer or poor person, and let no one harbor resentment for his brother’s wrong in your hearts.”

target_units.text: For if you truly correct your ways and practices and truly execute judgment between a man and his neighbor,
and do not oppress a newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm,
then I will settle you in this place, in the land I gave your fathers, from age to age.

triples.relationship: a disobedient back and refusal to hear God's instruction
triples.rationale: Zechariah depicts the people turning a senseless back and making their ears heavy. Nehemiah likewise recalls a disobedient back, stiffened necks and failure to hear God's law and prophets. Both use bodily images for deliberate refusal of instruction.
triples.source_text: But they refused to pay attention, turned a senseless back and made their ears heavy so as not to listen,

target_units.text: “Thou didst testify to them to turn them back to Thy law, but they did not listen. Instead, they sinned against Thy commandments and judgments, which, if a person does them, that person will live by them. They presented a disobedient back, stiffened their necks and did not listen.
“Thou didst prolong Thy dealings with them for many years and testify to them by Thy Spirit through Thy prophets, but they did not give ear. Thou gavest them into the hand of the peoples of the land.

triples.relationship: God's Spirit speaking through prophets whose words are ignored
triples.rationale: Zechariah says the Lord sent words by His Spirit through the former prophets, but the people would not listen. Nehemiah likewise recalls testimony by God's Spirit through prophets that the people did not heed. The shared means of communication and refusal are explicit.
triples.source_text: and made their heart disobedient, so as not to listen to My law and the words the Lord Almighty sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Great anger came from the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: “Thou didst prolong Thy dealings with them for many years and testify to them by Thy Spirit through Thy prophets, but they did not give ear. Thou gavest them into the hand of the peoples of the land.

triples.relationship: refusal to hear followed by unanswered appeals
triples.rationale: The Lord says that because the people ignored His speaking, He will not listen when they cry. In Proverbs, personified Wisdom similarly says that her ignored calls will be followed by calls she will not hear. The reciprocal refusal pattern is shared while the speaking voices remain distinct.
triples.source_text: It will be as He spoke and they did not listen to Him: so they will cry out, and I will certainly not listen, says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Since I kept calling and you did not obey, and kept extending words and you paid no attention,
but you were making my counsels ineffective and disobeyed my reproofs,
therefore I too will laugh at your ruin and exult when destruction comes to you,
and when sudden tumult reaches you and overthrow arrives like a storm, when affliction and siege come upon you, or when destruction comes to you.
For when you call upon me, I will not listen to you; evil people will seek me and will not find me,

triples.relationship: removal from the land and dispersion among nations
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces casting the people among unfamiliar nations and leaving the choice land desolate. Deuteronomy likewise warns of removal from the inherited land, scattering among nations and lack of rest there. Both join lost settlement with dispersion, preserving their different descriptions of what is unknown.
triples.source_text: I will cast them out among all the nations they did not know, and the land behind them will be obliterated, without anyone passing through or returning. They made a choice land a desolation.

target_units.text: And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.

And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.

And among those nations He shall give you no rest, neither shall there be a resting place for the sole of your foot; and the Lord shall give you there a faint heart, and failing eyes, and a wasting soul.

triples.relationship: same-book renewal of the declaration of jealousy for Zion
triples.rationale: The Lord's great jealousy for Jerusalem and Zion repeats the earlier announcement to Zechariah. The repeated named objects of His concern link the restoration promises, while this declaration also stresses great wrath.
triples.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy; with great wrath I have been jealous for her.

target_units.text: The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy,

triples.relationship: the Lord dwelling in Zion and Jerusalem's resulting holiness
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises the Lord's return to Zion and dwelling within Jerusalem, with His mountain called holy. Joel likewise names the Lord dwelling in Zion on His holy mountain and Jerusalem becoming a holy city. Both connect divine presence with the city's holy status.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord: I will return to Zion and dwell within Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the True City, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty a Holy Mountain.

target_units.text: You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.

triples.relationship: old age within the restored life of Jerusalem
triples.rationale: Zechariah pictures elderly people with staffs sitting again in Jerusalem's squares. Isaiah's promise of joy for Jerusalem likewise includes an old man completing his time. Both describe longevity within the restored city's life, without equating the stated ages or scenes.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women will again sit in Jerusalem’s squares, each holding a staff in hand because of many days.

target_units.text: I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.

There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.

triples.relationship: contrast between children playing and children failing in the city's squares
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises boys and girls playing throughout Jerusalem's squares. Lamentations depicts infants and nursing children failing from hunger in the city's squares. The shared setting and young inhabitants make the promised scene a concrete contrast to the lament's devastation.
triples.source_text: The city’s squares will be filled with boys and girls playing in her squares.

target_units.text: My eyes failed with tears; my heart was troubled. My glory was poured onto the ground at the shattering of the daughter of my people, as infant and nursing child failed in the city’s squares.
They said to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” They weakened like the wounded in the city’s squares, and their lives poured out into their mothers’ bosoms.

triples.relationship: human impossibility contrasted with God's ability
triples.rationale: Zechariah asks whether what seems impossible to the remnant must also be impossible to the Lord. In Genesis the Lord likewise challenges Sarah's doubt by asking whether any word is impossible with God. Both questions counter a human assessment of impossibility.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: If it is impossible before this people’s remnant in those days, surely it will not also be impossible before Me? says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And the Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh within herself, saying, ‘Shall I indeed bear a child, though I have grown old?’
Is any word impossible with God? At this season I will return to you, when the time comes round; and Sarah shall have a son.”

triples.relationship: gathering God's people from east and west
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises rescue from the eastern and western lands. Isaiah likewise promises bringing offspring from the east and gathering from the west, alongside other distant regions. The same opposing directions express the scope of gathering.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Look, I am rescuing My people from the eastern land and from the western land,

target_units.text: Do not fear, for I am with you. From the east I will bring your offspring, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north, ‘Bring them,’ and to the southwest, ‘Do not hinder. Bring My sons from a distant land and My daughters from the earth’s extremities,

triples.relationship: return to the land joined to the God-and-people covenant formula
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises bringing the people into Jerusalem and being their God while they are His people. Jeremiah likewise promises gathering the scattered, settling them confidently and the same mutual God-and-people relationship. Both join restored settlement with renewed belonging.
triples.source_text: and I will bring them in and dwell within Jerusalem. They will be My people, and I will be their God in truth and righteousness.

target_units.text: I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them in My anger, wrath, and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in confidence.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.

triples.relationship: strength for the community rebuilding the Lord's house
triples.rationale: Zechariah tells those hearing the rebuilding prophecies to let their hands be strong. Haggai likewise commands strength and work from Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people because the Lord and His Spirit are with them. Both encourage the temple-building community's labor.
triples.source_text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words in these days from the prophets’ mouth, from the day when the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and from when the temple was built.

target_units.text: But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,
and My Spirit stands in your midst. Take courage.

triples.relationship: wages that fail to benefit the workers
triples.rationale: Zechariah recalls a period when people's wages brought no benefit. Haggai likewise pictures earned wages gathered into a bundle with holes among the people's frustrated efforts. Both specifically describe ineffective wages in the rebuilding setting.
triples.source_text: Before those days people’s wages will bring no benefit, and animals’ hire will not exist; those going out or coming in will have no peace because of affliction. I will send everyone out against his neighbor.

target_units.text: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.

triples.relationship: same-chapter explanation of the change from former judgment to present good
triples.rationale: The Lord says He no longer acts toward the remnant as in former days. The later explanation contrasts His former intention to harm after provocation with His present intention to do good to Jerusalem and Judah. It states the change announced in this unit.
triples.source_text: Now I do not act toward this people’s remnant as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty,

target_units.text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: As I intended to harm you when your fathers provoked Me, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not change My mind,
so I have arrayed Myself and intended in these days to do good to Jerusalem and Judah’s house. Take courage.

triples.relationship: peace accompanied by fruitful land
triples.rationale: Zechariah joins peace with fruitful vines, earth's produce and heaven's dew. Leviticus likewise promises seasonal rain, land and tree produce, secure habitation and peace. Both combine agricultural abundance with peaceful settlement, while dew and rain retain their respective wording.
triples.source_text: but I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth its produce, and heaven its dew. I will give My people’s remnant all these as an inheritance.

target_units.text: then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
And your threshing shall reach the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall reach the sowing. You shall eat your bread to satisfaction and dwell securely in your land.
And war shall not pass through your land. I will give peace in your land. You shall lie down, with no one to frighten you, and I will destroy harmful animals from your land.

triples.relationship: reversal between withheld and bestowed agricultural provision
triples.rationale: Haggai describes heaven withholding dew and earth withholding produce. Zechariah promises heaven's dew and earth's produce for the remnant. The paired heaven-and-earth gifts make the later promise a specific contrast to the earlier deprivation.
triples.source_text: but I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth its produce, and heaven its dew. I will give My people’s remnant all these as an inheritance.

target_units.text: therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.

triples.relationship: encouragement of restored people whose disgrace becomes honor
triples.rationale: Zechariah tells Judah and Israel to take courage and strengthen their hands as preservation replaces their cursed condition. Zephaniah likewise tells Zion not to let her hands hang loose and promises reception, restored captivity and renown. Both join encouragement of the hands with reversal of the people's humiliation.
triples.source_text: As you were under a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will preserve you, and you will be in blessing. Take courage and be strong in your hands.

target_units.text: At that time the Lord will say to Jerusalem, “Take courage, Zion; do not let your hands hang loose.
The Lord your God is within you; mighty, He shall save you. He shall bring gladness upon you, and renew you in His love; and He shall rejoice over you with delight, as on a day of feasting.”
I will gather the crushed. Alas! Who took up reproach against her?
Look, I am acting within you for your sake at that time, says the Lord. I will save the oppressed and the rejected; I will receive them and make them a boast and renowned throughout the earth.

They will be ashamed at that time, when I do good to you and when I receive you. I will make you renowned and a boast among all the earth’s peoples, when I turn your captivity before you, says the Lord.

triples.relationship: former calamity recalled within a promise of new good
triples.rationale: Zechariah recalls the Lord's intention to harm after the fathers provoked Him, before announcing present good. Jeremiah likewise recalls the great calamities He brought and promises the good He has spoken. Both restoration declarations explicitly retain memory of divine judgment.
triples.source_text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: As I intended to harm you when your fathers provoked Me, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not change My mind,

target_units.text: For thus said the Lord: Just as I brought all these great calamities upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good things I spoke concerning them.

triples.relationship: the Lord's expressed intention to do good in restoration
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces the Lord's intention to do good to Jerusalem and Judah. Jeremiah likewise promises His attention to do the people good and plant them faithfully in the land. Both directly express that favorable purpose.
triples.source_text: so I have arrayed Myself and intended in these days to do good to Jerusalem and Judah’s house. Take courage.

target_units.text: I will attend to them to do them good and will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all heart and all soul.

triples.relationship: shared command to speak truth with one's neighbor
triples.rationale: Zechariah commands speaking truth, each to his neighbor, alongside peaceful judgment. Ephesians repeats the command to speak truth with one's neighbor while grounding it in mutual membership. The verbal ethical instruction closely corresponds.
triples.source_text: These are the things you shall do: speak truth, each to his neighbor, and render peaceful judgment in your gates.

target_units.text: Therefore, putting away falsehood, let each speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
